related_questions.question: What are the entry requirements for mental health nursing at the University of Hertfordshire?
related_questions.snippet: Entry requirements A first degree at Honours level, normally, in a related discipline (life sciences, psychology or the social/ behavioural sciences). Graduate attributes associated with learning and research skills will normally be expected. GCSE mathematics and English at grade C or above (or equivalent).

related_questions.question: What is psychotherapy in mental health nursing?
related_questions.snippet: Psychotherapy is an approach for treating mental health issues by talking with a psychologist, psychiatrist or another mental health provider. It also is known as talk therapy, counseling, psychosocial therapy or, simply, therapy.

related_questions.question: How to get into mental health nursing in the UK?
related_questions.snippet: You can do a degree in mental health nursing approved by the Nursing and Midwifery Council. You might be able to study another area of nursing alongside mental health nursing. You might be able to do a degree in mental health nursing and social work.

related_questions.question: How difficult is mental health nursing?
related_questions.snippet: Mental health nursing is different from any other kind of nursing because the many of the most important skills required are psychosocial - hard to apply consistently, hard to quantify and even harder to apply on the run. A great deal of mental discipline and self-assessment is required.
